Achieve collective breakthrough." **After**: Structured 3-step guide in a visually prominent box with icons and color coding #### ✅ GameScreen Improvements (During Gameplay) - [x] Increased instruction text size from `text-sm` to `text-lg/xl` for better visibility - [x] Added emojis for visual attention (⚠️ for alerts, 👆 for tapping) - [x] Enhanced contrast with stronger colors (text-red-400 instead of text-red-400/90) - [x] Added `font-bold` and `tracking-wide` for better readability - [x] Included two-line instructions: main action + explanatory sub-text - [x] Added border-t-2 to separate instructions from game area - [x] Increased background opacity (bg-black/80 instead of bg-black/60) - [x] Added `animate-pulse` effect to the word "GLOWING" for emphasis - [x] **Hints automatically hide at 10% coherence** - Instructions disappear when player reaches 10% coherence, reducing screen clutter once players understand the mechanics **Normal State (No Thought Bubbles) - Below 10% Coherence:** - Main: "👆 TAP THE GLOWING SIDE IN RHYTHM" - Sub-text: "Match the beat timing for better coherence" **At 10% Coherence or Higher:** - Hints automatically disappear, providing more screen space for gameplay **Infected State (With Thought Bubbles) - Below 10% Coherence:** - Main: "⚠️ TAP THE THOUGHT BUBBLE TO CLEAR IT" - Sub-text: "Click or tap the red bubble above to dismiss the intrusive thought" ### Mobile Scroll Fix Details (Final Solution): After several iterations to address scrolling issues on mobile Chrome/Android (specifically Google Pixel 10 Pro), settled on the simplest, most reliable approach: **Changes:** 1. author: exafto
body:
## Description

This PR adds a new plugin, harmonicmix, which calculates the harmonic compatibility between tracks. Playlist curators may use this to offer more harmonically coherent lists. DJs may use this to search for compatible songs around the same bpm as their current track.

This is my first contribution to Beets! I really enjoy using the tool and wanted to give back using my music theory knowledge. I hope this is helpful, and I am happy to make any changes needed to get this merged. My coding skills are not that sharp, so any feedback is much appreciated! I tried to follow community standards, but please let me know if I missed anything.

## Features:

- Harmonic Matching: Finds tracks compatible with the source song's key using the Circle of Fifths. For example, it is easy to move from a song in C to a song in F, G, or Am. It is really difficult to move to a song in G#.

- Enharmonic Support: Handles standard keys (e.g., C# and Db are treated as the same), as well as more nuanced options (like E#).

- BPM Filtering: Limits results to a mixable BPM range (+/- 8%).

## Future Improvements

- Make the BPM range configurable (currently fixed at +/- 8%).

- Integrate calls to autobpm and keyfinder to fill in missing metadata.

## To Do

- [x] Documentation.
- [x] Changelog.
- [x] Tests.

author: joschu
body:
## Human-Written Overview

This PR moves to making message content more structured. Previously we would typically have content strings with <think> or <function_calls> blocks inside, now we move towards using a list of content chunks. Our previous code was also inconsistent -- there was a thinking attribute on messages, which was only being used by gpt-oss and kimi. Now all the models are handled more uniformly.

This change will break a lot of code that assumes that content is a string, but I think it's for the best, in the long run. When I originally wrote the code, we were mostly dealing with the Qwen3 models and text-only data, and I figured that we should keep it simple until we have more use cases. Now with images and tool calling and a handful more models, the old string-based setup was getting really confusing, e.g., the rendering code had lots of string splitting and substitution.

---

## Summary

- Refactors how thinking/reasoning content is represented in `Message` type
- Moves from separate `thinking` field to `ThinkingPart` in the content list (similar to kosong's approach)
- Enables cleaner thinking stripping without string manipulation
- Adds `get_text_content()` helper for extracting text from messages after `parse_response`

## Changes

### Core refactor
- Add `ThinkingPart` TypedDict with `type: Literal["thinking"]` and `thinking: str`
- Update `ContentPart = TextPart | ImagePart | ThinkingPart | ToolCallPart | UnparsedToolCallPart`
- Remove `thinking` field from `Message` TypedDict
- Add `ensure_list()` utility to normalize content to list form
- Add `remove_thinking()` utility to filter out ThinkingPart elements
- Add `get_text_content()` utility to extract text from messages (stripping thinking)
- Update `GptOssRenderer` to parse multi-channel format into ThinkingPart/TextPart
- Update `KimiK2Renderer` to use `ensure_list` + `remove_thinking`
- Update `KimiK2Renderer.parse_response` to return `ThinkingPart` in content
- Update `Qwen3Renderer` to support `ThinkingPart` stripping via list filtering
- Update `DeepSeekV3ThinkingRenderer` to support `ThinkingPart` stripping
- Update `_preprocess_message_parts` to filter out ThinkingPart (VL renderers)

## Breaking Changes

1. **`Message.thinking` field removed**: Code that accesses `message["thinking"]` or `message.get("thinking")` will need to use the new utility functions or check the content list directly.

2. **`parse_response` may return list content**: For thinking models (Qwen3, DeepSeek, GptOss, KimiK2), when thinking/reasoning is present, `message["content"]` is now a list containing `ThinkingPart` and `TextPart` instead of a string.

3. **Code using `ensure_text` after `parse_response` may break**: If the model produces thinking content, `ensure_text(message["content"])` will fail. Use `get_text_content(message)` instead.

## Migration Guide

**Extracting text content after `parse_response`:**
```python
# Before (breaks with thinking models)
message, _ = renderer.parse_response(tokens)
content = ensure_text(message["content"])  # Fails if content is a list!

# After (works with all models)
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import get_text_content

message, _ = renderer.parse_response(tokens)
content = get_text_content(message)  # Extracts text, strips thinking
```

**Reading thinking from message:**
```python
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import ensure_list

parts = ensure_list(message["content"])
thinking = "".join(p["thinking"] for p in parts if p["type"] == "thinking")
text = "".join(p["text"] for p in parts if p["type"] == "text")
```

**Creating message with thinking:**
```python
from tinker_cookbook.renderers import ThinkingPart, TextPart

message = {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": [
        ThinkingPart(type="thinking", thinking="Let me think..."),
        TextPart(type="text", text="Hello"),
    ],
}
```

- [x] Type checking passes (pyright 0 errors)
- [x] Pre-commit checks pass
- [ ] Manual testing with thinking models

body:
## Why are these changes needed?

`DeprecationWarning` should be issued via `warnings.warn()`, not raised as an exception. When these removed modules (`ray.util.xgboost`, `ray.util.sgd`, `ray.util.lightgbm`) are imported, the intent is to fail the import with a helpful message.

Using `raise DeprecationWarning(...)` is incorrect because:
1. `DeprecationWarning` is a warning category, not an exception meant to be raised
2. When raised, it produces a confusing traceback instead of a clear import error
3. The correct approach for removed modules is to use `ImportError` which clearly indicates the import failed

This is a follow-up to PR #59697 which fixed the same issue in `ray.util.horovod` and `ray.experimental.dynamic_resources`.

## Related issue number

Similar to the pattern discussed in #59697.

The `--album-locked` option previously restricted to a single album, hiding the album selector entirely. This enhancement allows specifying multiple albums while maintaining security restrictions.

## Changes

**Argument parsing** (`args.py`)
- Changed `--album-locked` to accept multiple arguments via `nargs='+'`
- Albums stored as comma-separated list in environment variable

**Backend logic** (`routers/album.py`, `photomap_server.py`)
- Added `get_locked_albums()` helper to parse locked album list
- Updated `check_album_lock()` to validate against album list
- Modified `/available_albums/` to return only locked albums when restricted
- Main route validates URL `album` parameter against locked list
- **Startup validation**: Server validates all album keys exist in configuration before starting
  - Exits with error code 1 if any invalid album keys are specified
  - Exits with error code 1 if no albums are configured but `--album-locked` is used
  - Displays clear error messages listing invalid albums and available albums

**Frontend** (`templates/modules/settings.html`)
- Album selector shown when multiple albums locked, hidden for single album
- "Manage Albums" button hidden when any lock active

**Behavior:**
```bash
# Single album - selector hidden, management disabled
start_photomap --album-locked vacation

# Multiple albums - selector shows locked albums only, management still disabled  
start_photomap --album-locked vacation work_photos family

# URL parameter works with locked albums
http://localhost:8050?album=work_photos

# Invalid album - server exits with error
start_photomap --album-locked vacation nonexistent_album
# Error: The following album(s) specified in --album-locked do not exist in the configuration:
#   - nonexistent_album
# Available albums: vacation, work_photos, family
```

All filesystem operations, album management, and export functions remain disabled when any album lock is active.

**Testing:**
- Added unit test for validation logic
- All 49 backend tests pass
- Security scan completed with 0 alerts

author: emin-okic
body:
This PR introduces several improvements and refactors to the Prospect and Customer Details screens and their associated action toolbars.

For the Customer Details screen, the save button now only commits changes to the customer object without dismissing the sheet, allowing users to continue editing after saving. The screen maintains local editable copies of the customer’s full name and address, with proper detection of unsaved changes. Revert functionality is fully supported to discard edits and restore original data. Address changes trigger geocoding to update latitude and longitude automatically, and all edits generate automatic notes for audit purposes. The export-to-contacts feature and floating delete button remain fully functional, with improved feedback animations for export success.

For the Prospect Details screen, the edit flow and save behavior were aligned with best practices. The save button continues to commit changes but remains distinct from any sheet dismissal, allowing seamless editing. Local copies of the prospect’s full name and address are used to detect edits, and address changes trigger geocoding. Automatic notes are appended for name or address changes. The toolbar dynamically shows save and revert buttons only when edits are present.

Additionally, the action toolbars for both screens were refactored for clarity and consistency. Customer and prospect-specific actions, including adding appointments, deleting entries, and exporting contacts, were centralized and made more user-friendly. Tabs for Appointments, Knocks, and Notes were streamlined to improve readability and consistency across both screens.

Overall, these changes improve the UX by clearly separating edit/save actions from sheet dismissal, providing robust undo/revert functionality, and ensuring that updates to addresses and customer/prospect data are properly logged and persisted.

author: joseluispelayo
body:
This pull request introduces a new in-memory presence management system to track player/session positions and their associated zones, and integrates it throughout the WebSocket connection flow. The changes enhance how session presence is managed, updated, and cleaned up, and also add the ability to send zone snapshots to clients upon connection. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Presence Management System**

* Added the new `InMemoryPresence` class, which tracks session positions and zone presence, supports concurrent access, and provides atomic upsert/remove operations per session. It also enables building zone snapshots for clients. (`src/main/java/org/jpsoft/tfcws/infra/memory/InMemoryPresence.java`)
* Updated `SubscriptionService` to use `InMemoryPresence` for upserting presence when subscribing initial zones, and changed its API to return `Set<ChunkCoord>` instead of `Set<String>`. (`src/main/java/org/jpsoft/tfcws/app/subscription/SubscriptionService.java`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3d68cd87bbad1efd910afe154bf6b670abdb4486d667c31792161706517921b6R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3d68cd87bbad1efd910afe154bf6b670abdb4486d667c31792161706517921b6R36-R40) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3d68cd87bbad1efd910afe154bf6b670abdb4486d667c31792161706517921b6L50-R66)

**WebSocket Connection Flow Enhancements**

* Modified `OnConnectFlow` to use `InMemoryPresence` for tracking session presence and to send zone snapshots to the client after the initial subscription message. Introduced a new `MsgCodec` for encoding snapshot messages. (`src/main/java/org/jpsoft/tfcws/ws/OnConnectFlow.java`, `src/main/java/org/jpsoft/tfcws/ws/codec/MsgCodec.java`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0cc3b763cd032341f06443ef014591edeedbe0552d988fa90b30626f61855e1bR12-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0cc3b763cd032341f06443ef014591edeedbe0552d988fa90b30626f61855e1bL53-R71) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0cc3b763cd032341f06443ef014591edeedbe0552d988fa90b30626f61855e1bL101-R122) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0cc3b763cd032341f06443ef014591edeedbe0552d988fa90b30626f61855e1bL125-R150) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0cc3b763cd032341f06443ef014591edeedbe0552d988fa90b30626f61855e1bL214-R236) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-8e66b63bd9ad63169e229aff23c921547860759f07dd5b0266022d529ac3f326R1-R39)

**Session Cleanup on Disconnect**

* Enhanced `WsHandler` to remove session presence from `InMemoryPresence` when a WebSocket session ends, ensuring proper cleanup of session and zone data. (`src/main/java/org/jpsoft/tfcws/ws/WsHandler.java`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2067df348051cab9aff307562c56a9ad0459f792e299511f0ad05a0f56577c10R5-R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2067df348051cab9aff307562c56a9ad0459f792e299511f0ad05a0f56577c10R17) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2067df348051cab9aff307562c56a9ad0459f792e299511f0ad05a0f56577c10L47-R54) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2067df348051cab9aff307562c56a9ad0459f792e299511f0ad05a0f56577c10L90-R120)

These changes collectively improve session and zone tracking, concurrency safety, and client feedback with zone snapshots.

author: awesomekling
body:
We have a problem where some `HTML::Task` objects get stuck forever in the `HTML::TaskQueue` and never run, keeping entire realms alive.

I tracked down one cause of this issue, which was that we were scheduling tasks in inert temporary documents used for fragment parsing. Such documents by definition never become "fully active", and so all associated tasks will remain non-runnable.

We fix this in an ad-hoc way by just refusing to add such tasks to the task queues.

I've left a FIXME in there about following up on some ongoing spec work that aims to remove these inert temporary documents.

This prevents 5 `Task` leaks when running `test-web`, which were keeping one unnecessary realm alive.

Edit: tacked on another fix that stops leaking 10 more tasks, leaving only one stuck in the queue at the end of `test-web`.

body: ### Motivation - Allow users to open the Home Assistant more-info dialog from the compact sidebar now-playing card without using controls. - Make the artwork, title/artist area, and bottom icons act as click targets to view the configured entity details. - Ensure the clickable areas are visually discoverable by adding a pointer cursor. ### Description - Added a helper method ` _openMoreInfo()` that dispatches a `hass-more-info` event with the configured entity id. - Attached `@click=${this._openMoreInfo}` handlers to the artwork ``, the title block `.title`, and the icons row `.icons` in the `render()` output. - Added a `.clickable` CSS rule to set `cursor: pointer` and applied it to the three targets so the click areas cover the full visual element. - Changes made in `now-playing-sidebar-card.js` (no other files modified). ### Testing - No automated tests were run for this change. - The file was lint/committed locally and the change compiles as plain JS within the card file. ------ [Codex Task](https://chatgpt.com/codex/tasks/task_e_694f0bd69f648329b8af56433657237c)

author: hannahnchan
body:
### Motivation

- Allow users to create a board when none exist instead of silently auto-creating one so the UI can prompt for creation.
- Provide a simple per-column action to create tasks from the board UI.
- Ensure the notes editor shows when no board is linked and offers a relink action.

### Description

- Stop auto-creating boards in `src/features/api/boardService.ts` by returning `board: null` when none exists and add `createBoard` and `createTask` API helpers.
- Add a board empty-state form and `handleCreateBoard` logic in `src/features/board/components/Board.tsx`, plus `handleCreateTask` to create tasks and update local state.
- Add an `Agregar tarea` button to each column in `src/features/board/components/Column.tsx` which calls the new `onCreateTask` prop.
- Update `src/features/editor/QuillEditor.tsx` to surface when no board is available, add a `Vincular al tablero` button, and refactor note loading with `useCallback` and a loading flag.

### Testing

- Started the dev server with `npm run dev` and it launched successfully.
- Ran a Playwright smoke script that navigated to `http://127.0.0.1:4173/` and saved a screenshot (`artifacts/board-create.png`), which completed successfully.
- No automated unit or lint tests were run as part of this change.
